answer: Sybil resistance arises because bonded escrows make coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities sign conflicting statements, aggregate slashing grows quadratically, O(k^2), rather than linearly. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling operator, while asymmetric depreciation erodes remaining collateral. Thus a crystal or onyx identity cannot cheaply forge a swarm, since correlation turns apparent voting power into rapidly compounding liability.
